paper_title: Effect of thiophene/furan substitution on organic field effect transistor properties of arylthiadiazole based organic semiconductors
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Effect of thiophene_furan substitution on organic field effect transistor properties of arylthiadiazole based organic semiconductors/auto/Effect of thiophene_furan substitution on organic field effect transistor properties of arylthiadiazole based organic semiconductors.md

knowledge_points.content: The study synthesized four D-A type small molecules (T-NT-T, F-NT-F, T-BT-T, and F-BT-F) using benzothiadiazole (BT) or naphthothiadiazole (NT) as acceptor cores, flanked by thiophene (T) or furan (F) units and end-capped with 5-hexylthiophene.
knowledge_points.evidence: Therefore, we have chosen thiophene (T) and furan (F) for flanking groups along with naphthothiadiazole (NT) and benzothiadiazole (BT) for the conjugated core, while the flanking groups are end-capped with 5-hexylthiophene.

knowledge_points.content: Furan-containing molecules exhibit smaller dihedral angles and greater backbone planarity compared to their thiophene analogues due to the smaller atomic size of oxygen and reduced steric repulsion.
knowledge_points.evidence: It is notable that furan-containing molecules exhibit smaller dihedral angles than their thiophene analogues... In particular, the planarity of the molecules could be greatly enhanced by the addition of furan units.

knowledge_points.content: The T-BT-T based OFET device achieved the highest hole mobility among the studied materials, reaching a maximum value of 0.137 cm²/V·s.
knowledge_points.evidence: The T-BT-T based device I (Fig. 8a and d) showed a maximum hole mobility (μmax) of 1.37 × 10⁻¹ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

knowledge_points.content: Furan-substituted benzothiadiazole (F-BT-F) demonstrated a maximum hole mobility of 0.0122 cm²/V·s, proving furan is a viable building block for organic semiconductors.
knowledge_points.evidence: We successfully proved that a furan unit is a promising building block with a mobility (μmax) of 0.0122 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ for devices employing furan-substituted benzothiadiazole as the channel layer.

knowledge_points.content: The T-NT-T molecule was inactive in OFET devices because its high backbone twist (dihedral angles up to 50.3°) and unfavorable molecular alignment (b-axis aligned with current flow) inhibited charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the case of T-NT-T, the molecular packing was not appropriate for electrical conduction... the high backbone twist, which agrees with the inactive OFET performance when employing T-NT-T as the channel.

knowledge_points.content: Furan-substituted molecules (F-NT-F and F-BT-F) exhibit thermal decomposition temperatures (Td) of 342°C and 375°C respectively, which are comparable to their thiophene-based counterparts.
knowledge_points.evidence: The thermal decomposition temperatures (Td) were estimated to be 342, 359, 375, and 382 °C for F-NT-F, T-NT-T, F-BT-F, and T-BT-T, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Furan substitution significantly lowers the melting temperature (Tm) of the molecules (e.g., F-BT-F Tm = 112°C vs. T-BT-T Tm = 225°C), which may facilitate low-temperature solution processing.
knowledge_points.evidence: Furan containing molecules possessed a lower Tm compared to their thiophene analogues... Lowering of melting point by furan substitution seems to be effective when a given molecule exhibits too strong intermolecular interaction for low-temperature processing.

knowledge_points.content: Furan units can form 'conformational locks' through O–H (2.11–2.19 Å) and N–H (2.34–2.47 Å) intramolecular interactions, which stabilize the planar structure of F-NT-F.
knowledge_points.evidence: The furan ring adjacent to the NT core has two O–H (2.11–2.19 Å) and N–H (2.34–2.47 Å) bonds... The F-NT-F backbone structure can impose strong 'conformational locks' which causes the planarity and rigidity.

knowledge_points.content: A self-assembled monolayer (SAM) of 4-(dimethylamino)benzenethiol (DABT) was used to treat the gold electrodes in the bottom-gate bottom-contact (BGBC) OFETs to reduce the carrier injection barrier.
knowledge_points.evidence: 4-(Dimethylamino)benzenethiol (DABT) was used to create a covalent bond with the gold electrode prior to the organic semiconductor deposition. The dipole moment of this molecule will also modify the vacuum levels for the semiconductor.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) level show that the HOMO levels of furan-containing molecules are consistently higher than those of their thiophene analogues.
knowledge_points.evidence: The HOMO levels of the furan-containing molecules are always higher than those of the thiophene analogues, reflecting higher furan HOMO levels than those of thiophene.

knowledge_points.content: XRD analysis of thermally evaporated thin films revealed d-spacing values of 23.3 Å for F-BT-F and 17.3 Å for T-NT-T, indicating differences in molecular packing distance.
knowledge_points.evidence: the XRD patterns of the thermally evaporated thin films on the SiO2 substrate were collected... the corresponding d-spacing is reported in Table 3 [F-BT-F: 23.3, T-NT-T: 17.3].

knowledge_points.content: The naphthothiadiazole (NT) core results in a smaller energy band gap (Eg) and lower LUMO levels compared to the benzothiadiazole (BT) core due to the extended benzo group's stronger electron-accepting property.
knowledge_points.evidence: Compounds having the NT core exhibited a lower LUMO level which could be attributed to the stronger electron accepting properties that originate in the extended benzo group... the Eg of T-BT-T is the largest (2.27 eV) followed by F-BT-F (2.25 eV), T-NT-T (2.22 eV), and F-NT-F (1.95 eV).
